<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">


<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">December&nbsp;31,
2004, 15,000 shares of unvested restricted stock were forfeited and 9,384
shares of vested restricted stock were repurchased and cancelled. All of the
awards are expensed on a straight-line method over the scheduled vesting
period. The expected annual expense related to these grants in 2006 through
2007 is $1.7 million annually and $0.1 million in 2008. Compensation expense
related to the shares of restricted stock, which is included in the
consolidated statements of operations, was $1.5 million, $1.9&nbsp;million, and
$0.1 million for the years ended December&nbsp;31, 2005, 2004, and 2003,
respectively.</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(14)&nbsp;Commitments
and Contingencies<a name="a14CommitmentsAndContingencies_110410"></a></font></b></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;margin:6.0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(a)&nbsp;&nbsp; Loan
Commitments</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:6.0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">At both December&nbsp;31, 2005 and 2004, the Company
had origination commitments outstanding to fund approximately $422&nbsp;million
in mortgage loans. Fixed rate and hybrid ARM mortgages which are fixed for the
initial two to three year term of the loan, comprised 97.0% and 96.9%, respectively,
of the outstanding origination commitments. The Company had forward delivery
commitments to sell approximately $1.3&nbsp;billion and $0.4&nbsp;billion of
loans at December&nbsp;31, 2005 and 2004, respectively, of which
$26.6&nbsp;million and $63.1&nbsp;million, respectively, were mandatory sales
of mortgage-backed securities and investor whole loan trades. At December&nbsp;31,
2005 and 2004, the Company had a commitment to sell $580 million and
$40&nbsp;million, respectively, of treasury note forward contracts, used to
economically hedge the interest rate risk of its non-conforming loans.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;margin:6.0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(b)&nbsp;&nbsp; Office

<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">


<p style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(d)&nbsp;&nbsp; Legal Matters</font></i></b></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Arredondo
Litigation</font></u>:</b></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><font style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Arredondo, et al. v. Fieldstone Investment, et al.</font>, </font></i>is an action filed on August&nbsp;3,
2004 in the United States District Court for the District of Arizona by nine
former employees of Fieldstone Mortgage Company alleging that that their
supervisors and co-workers created a hostile work environment resulting from
gender discrimination, racial discrimination and retaliation in the workplace.
Plaintiffs claim that they are entitled to money damages in the form of back
pay and front pay and nominal, compensatory and punitive damages, costs and
attorney fees and equitable relief.</p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company filed its answer denying all relevant
claims on August&nbsp;25, 2004. In addition, the Company filed a variety of
motions seeking to have some of the plaintiffs dismissed from the lawsuit for
failure to exhaust their administrative remedies, to dismiss other claims as
not being permitted under the statute, and finally to sever the plaintiffs for
trial purposes. Plaintiffs filed a response to the Company&#146;s motion to dismiss,
sever or in the alternative, bifurcate, and on April&nbsp;18, 2005, the Company&#146;s
motion to dismiss was denied. The discovery process continues and is currently
required to be completed by the end of May&nbsp;2006. On December&nbsp;27,
2005, the named Plaintiff, Berinda Arredondo, requested to be, and was
dismissed from the litigation.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Due to the uncertain
nature of the litigation at this time, the Company is unable to estimate the
probable outcome of this matter. The plaintiffs in this matter have not
specified damages sought and therefore the Company is unable to estimate
potential exposure.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Bass Litigation</font></u>:</b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On May&nbsp;24, 2004, all of the Company&#146;s former
shareholders whose shares were redeemed following the closing of the 144A
Offering (the &#147;Former Shareholders&#148;), filed an action in the District Court of
Tarrant County, Texas, against the Company, Fieldstone Mortgage and KPMG LLP
(KPMG), alleging that the Former Shareholders whose shares were redeemed, for
approximately $188.1&nbsp;million, are entitled to an additional post-closing
redemption price payment of approximately $19.0 million. On September&nbsp;9,
2004, KPMG served its response to plaintiffs&#146; request for disclosure, stating,
among other things, that KPMG has determined that the deferred tax asset, which
is reflected in the Company&#146;s December&nbsp;31, 2003 audited financial
statements, should have been reflected in our financial statements as of November&nbsp;13,
2003, the day immediately prior to the closing of the 144A Offering. At the
present time, the ultimate outcome of this claim and the amount of liability,
if any, that may result is not determinable, and no amounts have been accrued
in the Company&#146;s financial statements with respect to this claim. On October&nbsp;28,
2005, the Company served a cross claim against KPMG. The Company&#146;s cross claim
asserts, among other claims, that KPMG&#146;s withdrawal of its audit report on the November&nbsp;13,
2003 balance sheet was improper and that due to this improper withdrawal the
Company suffered damages. In addition, the cross claim asserts that in the
event the Former Shareholders prevail in their suite, KPMG negligently advised
the Company regarding the November&nbsp;13, 2003 balance sheet giving rise to
this dispute. The cross claim seeks a judgment against KPMG in an amount in
excess of $1 million, plus prejudgment interest for the attorneys fees and
costs incurred in this lawsuit.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company intends to vigorously
defend against the claim made by the Former Shareholders described above. If
the Company ultimately is unsuccessful in defending this matter, the Company
could be required to make a cash payment of up to $19.0&nbsp;million to the Former
Shareholders, plus potential interest and third-party costs associated with the
litigation. Excluding interest or third-party costs, which may be payable as
part of a settlement, the potential payment will be an increase in the redemption
price of their shares and recorded as a reduction of the Company&#146;s paid in
capital in the period in which the dispute is resolved and will be paid out of
its working capital and will not be reflected in the Company&#146;s income
statement.</font></p>


 <p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:24.0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">F-</font><font face="Times New Roman">32</font></p> <br><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="center">

<!-- SEQ.=1,FOLIO='F-32',FILE='C:\fc\104135618793_D11854_1028717\2061-1-fy.htm',USER='jmsproofassembler',CD='Apr 14 13:57 2006' -->
<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">


<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Rhodes Litigation</font></u>:</b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On January&nbsp;9, 2006, a class action lawsuit was
filed naming Fieldstone Mortgage in the Northern District of Illinois (Eastern
Division) alleging violations of the Fair Credit Reporting Act. &#160;The class action is entitled Rhodes v.
Fieldstone Mortgage Company. Plaintiff alleges that Fieldstone Mortgage
violated the firm offer of credit guidelines encapsulated in 15 U.S.C. &#167;1681 et
seq. during its mail marketing campaign in or around April&nbsp;2005. In
specific, Plaintiff alleges that Fieldstone Mortgage did not comply with the
statutory guidelines in providing a firm offer of credit to the potential
consumer. Pursuant to 15&nbsp;U.S.C. &#167;1681 et seq., statutory damages can range
from $100 to $1,000 per mailing in the event that the violation is deemed
willful. No motion for class certification has yet been filed in this case. Fieldstone
Mortgage filed a motion to dismiss/motion to strike pursuant to Federal Rule&nbsp;12(b)(6)&nbsp;for
the injunction relief portion of the compliant. Fieldstone Mortgage&#146;s discovery
responses are due by the end of April&nbsp;2006.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Due to the uncertain nature of the litigation at this
time, the Company is unable to estimate the probable outcome of this matter.
While the Company intends to continue to vigorously defend this claim and
believes that it has meritorious defenses available, there can be no assurance
that the Company will prevail and that an adverse outcome would not have a
material effect on the Company&#146;s results of operations.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In addition to the matters
described above, because the nature of the Company&#146;s business involves the
collection of numerous accounts, the validity of liens and compliance with
various state and federal lending and consumer protection laws, the Company is
subject to various legal proceedings in the ordinary course of our business
related to foreclosures, bankruptcies, condemnation and quiet title actions and
alleged statutory and regulatory violations. The Company is also subject to
other legal proceedings in the ordinary course of business. All of these
ordinary course proceedings, taken as a whole, are not expected to have a
material adverse effect on the Company&#146;s business, financial condition or
results of operations.</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(15)&nbsp;Employee
Benefit Plans<a name="a15EmployeeBenefitPlans_110805"></a></font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company maintains a 401(k)&nbsp;savings plan (the
Plan) in which all eligible employees may participate after completing a period
of service with the Company. The Company&#146;s policy is to match a percentage of
an employee&#146;s contribution to the Plan. The Company may change the match
percentage from time to time. The Company&#146;s contributions to the Plan become
vested after an employee completes a period of service with the Company. For
the years ended December&nbsp;31, 2005, 2004, and 2003, the Company contributed
$2.2 million, $1.9&nbsp;million, and $1.8&nbsp;million, respectively.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company maintains a Section&nbsp;125 cafeteria
plan for medical and childcare expenses. All full time employees are eligible
to participate in the cafeteria plan after completing a period of service with
the Company.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Effective July&nbsp;2002,
the Board of Directors approved the adoption of an employee incentive and
retention bonus plan (the Incentive Plan) for eligible senior management (the
Participants.) Under the Incentive Plan, the Board of Directors may, at its
discretion, periodically establish an aggregate amount to be awarded to the
Participants, to be paid at a defined date, subject to their continued
employment over a defined period of time. The Company has recorded $2.0 million,
$1.3&nbsp;million, and $2.1&nbsp;million of expense for the deferred
compensation portion of these obligations under this Incentive Plan for the
year ended December&nbsp;31, 2005, 2004, and 2003, respectively. In 2003, the
Company paid $0.6&nbsp;million of accrued bonus relating to the deferred
compensation portion of the Plan to the retired chief executive officer and
chairman and $16.2&nbsp;million of expense relating to the change of control
component of the Plan to eligible senior management.</font></p>


 <p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:24.0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">F-</font><font face="Times New Roman">33</font></p>
</div><br><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="center">

<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">

<div>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><a name="a16DisclosuresOfFairValueOfFinanc_110813"></a><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(16)&nbsp;Disclosures
of Fair Value of Financial Instruments</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The assumptions used and the estimates disclosed
represent management&#146;s best judgment of appropriate valuation methods. These
estimates are based on pertinent information available to management as of
December&nbsp;31, 2005 and 2004. In certain cases, fair values are not subject
to precise quantification or verification and may change as economic and market
factors, and management&#146;s evaluation of those factors change.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Although management uses its best judgment in
estimating the fair value of these financial instruments, there are inherent
limitations in any estimation technique. Therefore, these fair value estimates
are not necessarily indicative of the amounts that the Company would realize in
a market transaction. It is important that the many uncertainties discussed
above be considered when using the estimated fair value disclosures and to
realize that because of these uncertainties, the aggregate fair value amount
should in no way be construed as representative of the underlying value of the
Company.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(a) Cash and
Restricted Cash</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The carrying amount of cash and restricted cash
approximates its fair value.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(b)&#160; Mortgage
Loans Held for Sale, Net</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The estimated fair value of mortgage loans held for
sale was determined by investor commitment prices for those loans allocated to
a specific commitment. The fair value of loans not allocated to a specific
commitment was estimated using current market pricing for similar assets.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(c)&#160; Mortgage
Loans Held for Investment, Net</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The estimated fair value for mortgage loans held for
investment was determined by obtaining dealer quotes for a whole loan sales
price for the portfolio loan product.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(d)&#160; Accrued
Interest Receivable and Interest Payable</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The carrying amount of accrued interest receivable and
accrued interest payable approximates fair value because these instruments are
of short duration and do not present significant credit concerns.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(e)&#160; Derivative
Instruments</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The estimated fair value of derivative instruments is
estimated by discounting projected future cash flows at appropriate rates and
by obtaining dealer quotes.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(f)&#160; Warehouse
Financing</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The carrying amount
of warehouse financing approximates its fair value due to its variable rate.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(g)&#160; Securitization
Financing</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Securitization financing is secured by mortgage loans
held for investment and is tied to one month LIBOR and accordingly, carrying
value is considered a reasonable estimate of fair value.</font></p>


 <p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:12.0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">F-</font><font face="Times New Roman">34</font></p> <br><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="center">

Requirements</b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">FMC is
subject to a number of minimum net worth requirements resulting from
contractual agreements with secondary market investors and state-imposed
regulatory mandates. The most stringent net worth requirement is imposed upon
FMC by the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) in connection
with Federal Housing Authority loans originated by FMC. The table below
summarizes the HUD net worth requirements of FMC as of December&nbsp;31, 2005

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 20.0pt;text-indent:-20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">*&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; Income tax
(expense) benefit, net income (loss) and earnings (loss) per share of common
stock for the four quarters of 2004 and the first three quarters of 2005 have
been restated.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company has restated its quarterly financial
results for each of the four quarters in the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2004
and each of the first three quarters in the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2005. See
related discussion of the restatement in Note 1(w).</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 20.0pt;text-indent:-20.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">(19)&#160;
Subsequent Event</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On January&nbsp;13, 2006, the Board of Directors of
the Company approved a plan of disposal to sell, close or otherwise dispose of
the assets of the Company&#146;s conforming retail and conforming wholesale segments.
On January&nbsp;16, 2006, FMC entered into an agreement with a third party to
sell certain personal property and contract rights pertaining to FMC&#146;s
conforming division&#146;s headquarters office in San Antonio, Texas, the conforming
division&#146;s wholesale offices and certain of its retail offices. On February&nbsp;28,
2006, the Company closed on the agreement with this third party. As of December&nbsp;31,
2005 the carrying amount of the furniture, equipment and leasehold improvements
owned by FMC and the value of security deposits relating to the offices
acquired was approximately $0.3 million. The Company estimates its pre-tax
expenses related to these transactions to be approximately $1.0 million.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On February&nbsp;17, 2006, FMC sold certain personal
property and contract rights pertaining to two retail conforming offices to
another third party.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The remaining assets of the conforming segment, which
include retail offices in Maryland and Virginia, have been combined with the
Company&#146;s non-conforming retail offices and will offer a range of
non-conforming and conforming loan products.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;line-height:9.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 2.0pt 20.0pt;text-indent:-20.0pt;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:8.0pt;">(1)</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="1" style="font-size:8.0pt;">Mortgage loans held for investment primarily consist of
non-conforming, adjustable-rate, first lien loans.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;line-height:8.5pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt 20.0pt;text-indent:-20.0pt;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:8.0pt;">(2)</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="1" style="font-size:8.0pt;">As of December&nbsp;31, 2005, 98.5% of the mortgage
loans held for investment will contractually mature during the years of 2033
through 2036.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 2.0pt;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:8.0pt;">NOTES:</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;margin:0pt 0pt 2.0pt 20.0pt;text-indent:-20.0pt;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:8.0pt;">(1)</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="1" style="font-size:8.0pt;">Mortgage loans held for investment primarily
consist of non-conforming, adjustable-rate, first lien loans.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt 20.0pt;text-indent:-20.0pt;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:8.0pt;">(2)</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="1" style="font-size:8.0pt;">As of December&nbsp;31, 2004, 99.9% of the
mortgage loans held for investment will contractually mature during the years
of 2033 through 2035.</font></p>
